name: terminal_use
description: Run a command inside the persistent pty terminal opened by `terminal_create`. Fails fast with "Error: Terminal not created, please use terminal_create tool to create one first" if called before terminal_create. State (cwd, exported vars, aliases, active ssh/python REPL) persists between calls — this is the tool to use when a workflow needs shared environment across steps. Each call appends a structured footer: `[exit N, duration Ns, foreground=…]` when the sentinel fires, `[no exit captured — output idle …]` when the shell is parked waiting for input (e.g. inside a REPL), or `[timed out after Ns …]` on the hard cap. When the environment fingerprint (venv / cwd / git branch) changes between calls, the output is prefixed with `[env: <venv> | path: <cwd> | git: <branch>]` so you notice the drift without re-probing. Not for long-running background processes — use `bash(run_in_background=true)` for those.

command.description: Shell command (or input for whatever subprocess currently owns the pty, e.g. a line to type into a python REPL after `python3` was launched in an earlier call).

timeout.description: Hard total-time cap in seconds (default 60). On expiry ^C is sent through the pty to the foreground process group; the shell remains alive.

idle_threshold.description: Seconds of output-idle that count as 'command done waiting for input' (default 1.5). Shorter = faster return for interactive commands; longer = more room for slow-streaming output. Most callers leave this unset.
